issues.legal_issue: An express undertaking incorporated into a court order is not reduced to a mere consent order because it induced the parties to agree to the order, and its deliberate breach may constitute contempt of court.
material_facts: The order recorded an express undertaking to vacate the premises after notice, along with undertakings concerning payment and possession.
The court dismissed the pending proceeding in view of the undertakings, which were recorded as undertakings to the court.
After receiving the required notice, the litigant did not comply with the undertaking and argued that the order was merely an agreement between the parties.
The High Court convicted the litigant of contempt, and the matter came before the Supreme Court as an appeal from that conviction.
issues.conclusion: The order contained express undertakings to the court, not merely an agreement with an order appended to it. Their deliberate breach amounted to contempt, and the conviction was affirmed.
issues.legal_principle: Under Section 19(1)(b) of the Contempt of Courts Act, 1971, the conviction was appealable. Halsbury’s Laws of England, 4th ed., Vol. 9, paras. 71 and 75, and Dashwood v. Dashwood (1927) distinguish breach of a mere consent order from breach of an express undertaking in an order. A breach of a mere consent order ordinarily calls for specific performance or an injunction before contempt proceedings; an express undertaking in the order may support an immediate contempt application. An undertaking given to the court on the faith of which the court sanctions a course of action has the same force as an injunction, and its breach may amount to contempt.

rule.if: appeal_from_contempt_conviction and express_undertaking_in_order and court_acted_in_reliance and undertaking_breached and deliberate_breach

predicates.appeal_from_contempt_conviction: The matter is an appeal from a conviction for contempt of court.
predicates.express_undertaking_in_order: A litigant gave an express undertaking to the court that was incorporated into its order.
predicates.court_acted_in_reliance: The court sanctioned a course of action in reliance on the undertaking.
predicates.undertaking_breached: The litigant failed to do what the undertaking required.
predicates.deliberate_breach: The litigant deliberately failed to comply with the undertaking.

issues.definition: When an appeal from a contempt conviction concerns a deliberate breach of an express undertaking incorporated into an order on which the court relied, the breach is treated as contempt.

issues.legal_issue: A litigant’s surrender of possession after contempt proceedings begin does not undo the contempt already committed by breaching a court undertaking.
material_facts: The litigant failed to vacate after receiving the notice that triggered the undertaking to vacate.
The litigant surrendered possession only after contempt proceedings had been initiated.
issues.conclusion: The later surrender of possession made no difference to the initial wrong and did not undo the contempt.
issues.legal_principle: The court held that the effect of a deliberate violation of an undertaking to the court was the same as breach of an injunction; subsequent compliance after contempt proceedings began did not alter the initial breach.

predicates.contempt_proceeding: Contempt proceedings were initiated concerning a litigant’s breach of an undertaking to the court.
predicates.undertaking_breached: The litigant failed to do what the undertaking required.
predicates.possession_surrendered_after_proceedings: The litigant surrendered possession after the contempt proceedings had begun.

issues.definition: If a litigant breaches an undertaking and surrenders possession only after contempt proceedings begin, the surrender does not undo the contempt.
